root_cause.text: Clearing the RTF_ADDRCONF flag from an existing IPv6 route that has a gateway makes it eligible for ECMP, but the route was never added to the fib6_siblings list, leading to a sibling count mismatch that triggers a kernel BUG in fib6_add_rt2node().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "When RTF_ADDRCONF is cleared from a route that has a gateway, that route becomes eligible for ECMP, i.e. rt6_qualify_for_ecmp() returns true. The issue is that this route was never added to the fib6_siblings list" and that "When a subsequent ECMP route is added, fib6_add_rt2node() hits BUG_ON(sibling->fib6_nsiblings != rt->fib6_nsiblings)". The patch adds the condition `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to prevent clearing the flag on routes with a gateway.

The issue is that this route was never added to the fib6_siblings list" and that "When a subsequent ECMP route is added, fib6_add_rt2node() hits BUG_ON(sibling->fib6_nsiblings != rt->fib6_nsiblings)". The patch adds the condition `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to prevent clearing the flag on routes with a gateway.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug where adding a route without ADDRCONF/PREFIX_RT flags could incorrectly clear those flags from an existing route that has a gateway.
intent_record.what: Added an additional condition `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to the if statement that clears RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT flags from an existing route when adding a new route.
intent_record.how: The flags are now only cleared if the new route does not have ADDRCONF or PREFIX_RT and the existing route has no gateway (next hop gateway family is zero). Existing routes with a gateway will retain the flags even if the new route lacks them.

grouping_result.intent: Fix a bug where adding a route without ADDRCONF/PREFIX_RT flags could incorrectly clear those flags from an existing route that has a gateway.

relevance_review.reason: The group fixes the bug where adding a route could incorrectly clear the RTF_ADDRCONF flag from an existing route with a gateway, which is the exact trigger for the ECMP sibling count mismatch and kernel BUG described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This condition allows clearing the RTF_ADDRCONF flag from an existing route if the new route does not have the flags, without checking whether the existing route has a gateway. This can make the existing route eligible for ECMP despite never being added to the fib6_siblings list.

Clearing the RTF_ADDRCONF flag from an existing route that has a gateway makes it eligible for ECMP. Since the route was never added to the fib6_siblings list, the sibling count becomes mismatched, leading to a kernel BUG.

Clearing the RTF_PREFIX_RT flag is part of the same buggy block. Although the root cause focuses on RTF_ADDRCONF, removing RTF_PREFIX_RT may also contribute to the vulnerability by altering the route's properties.

vuln_statements.explanation: The condition allows clearing RTF_ADDRCONF from an existing route (iter) when the new route (rt) does not have those flags, without checking if the existing route has a gateway. This makes it eligible for ECMP despite not being in the fib6_siblings list.

Clearing RTF_ADDRCONF from an existing route that has a gateway makes it eligible for ECMP. Since the route was never added to the fib6_siblings list, the sibling count mismatches, leading to a kernel BUG.

Clearing RTF_PREFIX_RT is part of the same buggy block. Although the root cause focuses on RTF_ADDRCONF, this alteration of route properties contributes to the vulnerability by further modifying the route's flags.
